entities.name: Alcetas
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alcetas, son of Orontes from Orestis and brother of Perdiccas, emerged as a significant, albeit ultimately unsuccessful, military commander in the tumultuous aftermath of Alexander the Great's death (323 BCE). Initially distinguished as one of Alexander's generals during the Indian campaigns, Alcetas's historical importance stems from his direct involvement in the Wars of the Diadochi, the brutal succession conflicts that tore apart the vast Macedonian Empire. His career exemplifies the volatile period when Alexander's former companions vied for control, shaping the geopolitical landscape of the Hellenistic Age.

Following Alexander's demise, Alcetas remained a staunch loyalist to his brother Perdiccas, who initially served as regent for the nominal kings Philip III Arrhidaeus and Alexander IV. Alcetas actively participated in the defense of Perdiccas's regency, notably in the campaign against Ptolemy in Egypt. After Perdiccas's assassination in 321 BCE, Alcetas inherited his brother's army and continued to resist the new regency established by Antipater. He allied with Eumenes of Cardia, another prominent Perdiccan loyalist, and for several years commanded independent forces in Asia Minor, engaging in a complex series of skirmishes and alliances against Antigonus I Monophthalmus, the dominant power in the region. His independent actions included the assassination of Cynane, half-sister of Alexander the Great, in 322 BCE, an act that further destabilized the regency.
